wins.label: Strong Organic Growth
wins.evidence: Our strategy to anchor our business and structural growth engines like private markets, ETFs, digital assets, whole portfolio solutions, systematic and tax-managed strategies and technology, that strategy helped again deliver above target 6% organic base fee growth.

wins.label: Margin Expansion
wins.evidence: 100 basis points of margin expansion in the first quarter of 2025.

wins.label: Record AUM and Inflows
wins.evidence: We finished the record quarter with record AUM, record units of trust of $11.6 trillion.

wins.label: Diversified Growth
wins.evidence: Net inflows and organic base fee growth were well diversified across the entire BlackRock platform.

wins.label: Strategic Acquisitions
wins.evidence: We've built our business around structural growers, ETFs, private markets, tax managed and systematic, data-driven investing and whole portfolio solutions.

risks.label: Market Volatility
risks.evidence: Markets may take some time to sort out saber-rattling around trade and tariffs.

risks.label: Regulatory Uncertainty
risks.evidence: We do think of ourselves as a U.S. firm with international offices. We're a European firm. We're a Canadian firm. We're a Middle Eastern firm.

risks.label: Geopolitical Tensions
risks.evidence: We're in a period of geopolitical and economic activity, but we have seen this before.

risks.label: Client Redemptions
risks.evidence: Institutional index net outflows of $46 billion were concentrated in low fee index equities.

risks.label: Regulatory Delays
risks.evidence: We do think for the opportunity to be really broad, really scalable and the most tangible, we'd likely need to see litigation reform or at least some advice reform in the U.S.

wins.label: Strong Organic Base Fee Growth
wins.evidence: BlackRock surpassed its 5% organic base fee growth target even with more stressed and uncertain markets.

wins.label: Record AUM and Assets Under Management
wins.evidence: BlackRock finished the record quarter with record AUM, record units of trust of $11.6 trillion.

wins.label: Diversified Net Inflows
wins.evidence: Net inflows were approximately $140 billion, excluding episodic institutional index equity activity.

wins.label: Private Market Growth
wins.evidence: Aggregate $7 billion of net inflows led by infrastructure and private credit.

wins.label: ETF Growth
wins.evidence: ETF net inflows of $107 billion were positive across all channels led by core equity and fixed income ETFs.

risks.label: Market Volatility
risks.evidence: The S&P 500 ended 9% off its February peak during the quarter.

risks.label: Institutional Index Equity Outflows
risks.evidence: Institutional index net outflows of $46 billion were concentrated in low fee index equities.

risks.label: Performance Fees Decline
risks.evidence: Performance fees decreased from a year ago, primarily reflecting lower performance revenue from private markets and liquid alternatives.

risks.label: Technology Expenses
risks.evidence: Total expense increased 10% year-over-year, reflecting higher sales, asset and account, G&A and compensation expense.

risks.label: Interest Rate Risk
risks.evidence: The steepening yield curve could drive more capital flows into private markets as investors look to insulate portfolios from tariff impacts and seek attractive income and growth.
